stem: In a one-period binomial model, the up factor is 1.15, the down factor is 0.90 and the risk-free rate per period is 3%. The risk-neutral probability of an up move is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 0.48 is the risk-neutral probability of a down move, 1 − π.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 0.50 assumes equal probabilities instead of computing them from u, d and r.

stem: A share trades at USD 100. In one year it will be either USD 120 or USD 90. The annual risk-free rate is 4%. Using a one-period binomial model, the value of a one-year European call with an exercise price of USD 100 is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 9.33 is the risk-neutral expected payoff before discounting at the risk-free rate.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 9.62 uses a 50% probability of an up move instead of the risk-neutral probability.

stem: Using the same tree (share at USD 100 moving to USD 120 or USD 90) and a call with an exercise price of USD 100, the number of shares that must be bought per call written to form a riskless portfolio is closest to:

rationale.B: Incorrect. 0.47 is the risk-neutral probability of an up move, not the hedge ratio.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 1.50 inverts the ratio (change in share price divided by change in option value).

stem: In a one-period binomial model, an analyst raises her estimate of the real-world probability that the share price will rise, while the current share price, the up and down factors and the risk-free rate are unchanged. The no-arbitrage value of a call option will most likely:
options: increase, because the call pays off in the up state
decrease, because the risk-neutral probability falls
explanation: The option is priced by replication using the share and a risk-free bond. Its value depends on S0, u, d, r and X, not on real-world probabilities, which are already reflected in the current share price.

rationale.A: Incorrect. Real-world probabilities do not enter the no-arbitrage valuation; only the risk-neutral probability does.
rationale.B: Correct. With S0, u, d and r unchanged, the risk-neutral probability and the replicating portfolio are unchanged, so the call value is unchanged.
rationale.C: Incorrect. The risk-neutral probability depends only on u, d and r, none of which has changed.
